title: Nonprofit hospitals spend billions on consultants with no clear effect
summary: Research reveals that nonprofit hospitals in the US are spending billions of dollars on management consultants, yet there's limited evidence showing these expenditures improve patient outcomes or reduce costs. The study from University of Chicago Medicine highlights transparency concerns and questions about the value these consulting firms provide to healthcare organizations.
problem_solved: Investigates whether massive spending by nonprofit hospitals on management consultants actually delivers measurable benefits to patients or healthcare quality.
why_valuable: Sheds light on how nonprofit hospitals allocate resources and whether current consulting expenditures serve their charitable mission or merely enrich management.
